title: the board shows intent cards: a before/after node drawing in fm-diagram.sh, the intent sections with read-only STE checks, and confirm questions whose 'No, change it' answer becomes a spec-change request
acceptance: Why. T-210 adds intent cards (optional intent fields in the decision details, checked against ASD-STE100 when the card is raised, with an `ste` report stored on the pending record) but nothing shows them: the board card (board/public/index.html, `full` about :683-716) renders only title, explanation, the diagram iframe, before -> after text, gates and A/B/C, and bin/fm-diagram.sh's built-in tier (about :353-361) draws only the before/after text as two paragraphs, so a card has no drawing of what changes unless someone hand-authors design/diagrams/D-*.html. The captain approved the prototype (the 'Intent Card Prototype' artifact) that adds a before/after node flow, the intent sections, a per-sentence STE check and confirm questions. This task renders all of it and records the captain's answers to confirm questions. Defaults the captain left open, each changeable later by a card: a 'No, change it' answer turns the answer into a spec-change request, never a dispatch or merge; no light theme; cards only.

Record shapes this task reads (defined by T-210, design/tasks/T-210.json, which this task depends on; restated here so the spec stands alone). The pending record (state/pending/<id>.json) has `details` and, for an intent card only, `ste` next to it. Per locale under `details.en` and `details["zh-TW"]` (an intent card has `intent` in both locales; every optional field is present in both or neither): `intent`, `why`, `done`, `questions`: arrays of {kind: 'step'|'fact', text}; `scope_in`, `scope_out`: arrays of strings; `notes`: array of {kind: 'note'|'caution', text}; `before_nodes`, `after_nodes`: arrays of {state: 'same'|'gone'|'new', label} ('gone' only before, 'new' only after; same counts in both locales); `change_table`: array of {text, A, B, C} with each cell one of '✓', '—', '?'; `questions` has 1-6 items and the same count in both locales. `ste` = {intent_card: true, ok: bool, locales: {en: [entry...], "zh-TW": [entry...]}, labels: {en: [entry...], "zh-TW": [entry...]}} with entry = {field, index (integer or null), sentence, kind, n, max, issues: [{rule, detail, severity: 'fail'|'warn'}]}; `field` is the details key the sentence came from (e.g. 'intent', 'explanation', 'options.A.pros'), `index` its array position. The page takes chips for a zh-TW (and zh-CN) sentence from `ste.locales["zh-TW"]` and for English from `ste.locales.en`, matching on field and index; the STE pill shows passed/total over that locale's entries (passed = no fail issue). The rule table comes from `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py rules` as merged by T-210 (on this task's base, since it depends on T-210); the page uses only each rule's id and its en / zh-TW text from that output, under whatever key names T-210's merged module uses.

fm-diagram.sh, built-in tier (bin/fm-diagram.sh `render`, about :307-361): when the pending record's `details[<lang>]` has `before_nodes` and `after_nodes` and no authored tier applies (authored drawings in design/diagrams/ still win, unchanged), render, inside the existing `.before-after` container, two `<section>`s with an arrow between them, each holding an inline SVG flow in the style of the authored tier: viewBox `0 0 300 <h>`, one rect per node top to bottom (height 24, gap 12, rx 4) joined by short down arrows; state 'same' = stroke var(--line), label var(--fg2); 'gone' = stroke var(--bad) dashed `4 2`, faint red fill, a `✕` at the right; 'new' = stroke var(--brass), faint brass fill, a `+` at the right; each SVG has role=img and its accessible name in a `<title>` child element whose text node is the labels joined by ' → ' (a text node, so the zh-CN conversion of text nodes converts it; no aria-label attribute, because attributes are copied unconverted), and each node label is an SVG `<text>` element. Under each SVG the existing before/after text paragraph stays. Under the pair: a legend (three swatches with dictionary words for no change / the problem, removed / new or changed) and, when `change_table` is present, a table with header row (dictionary 'Change', A, B, C) and one row per entry; cells '✓' in var(--ok), '—' in var(--fg3), '?' in var(--warn). The colour for 'gone' (#f2645a) and every new style (node flow, legend, change table) are written only on pages that draw nodes: as inline attributes on the SVG elements and table cells, or in a second `<style>` block emitted only when nodes are drawn; the shared `:root`/`<style>` block printed for every page is not changed, so a page without nodes is byte-identical to base. Every label and table text goes through the existing `esc`; nothing from the record reaches markup unescaped. zh-CN is derived from the zh-TW page as today (text nodes only). Records without nodes render exactly as today (text-only tier, or missingDetails). New dictionary keys go in i18n/ui.en.json and i18n/ui.zh-TW.json (zh-CN derived): e.g. lgSame, lgGone, lgNew, change2 (names are the worker's choice; tests/i18n.test.sh's parity rules apply), plus the server code `answersInvalid` (tests/i18n.test.sh:48-52 requires every code the server sends to be a key in both dictionaries) whose page message says every question needs an answer and every 'No' needs text, and the 'change requested' label.

The board card (board/public/index.html `full`): for a card whose `details` has `intent` (an intent card), after the existing explanation, diagram embed, before -> after fallback and outcome text, add a section headed by a dictionary word for 'Intent alignment (STE)' showing, in the reader's language (zh-CN through the existing tw2cn conversion): intent, why, scope in / scope out (two lists), done when, notes and cautions (each in its own box: note in var(--warn), caution in var(--bad)), and the confirm questions. Each sentence of intent/why/done/notes/questions is shown with read-only chips taken from the record's `ste` report (kind, `n/max` words, the failing or warning rule ids, or ✓) — the page never recomputes the rules; a card whose `ste` is missing shows the sections without chips. The card header shows a pill 'STE · <passed>/<total>' from the report. The rule texts for chip tooltips come from the JSON that `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py rules` prints (T-210): the server runs `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py rules` once at start and serves `ste_rules` in /api/state as an array of {id, en, "zh-TW"} (the rule id and its English and Traditional Chinese text), mapped from T-210's output keys; when the command is missing or fails, `ste_rules` is an empty array and chips show the rule id without a tooltip text, never a broken page. The page builds each chip's tooltip as `<id> — <text in the reader's language>` (zh-CN through tw2cn) and holds no copy of the rules. Tests run with the real module (this task's base contains T-210): the e2e fixture tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts (about :93-98) builds a temporary FM_ROOT from a fixed bin/lib list, so add `fm_ste.py` to that list (it imports only json, re and sys, so nothing else is needed); and one case with the module absent (empty `ste_rules`, chips still render ids). The mapping from T-210's `rules` output `{rules:[{id, text:{en, "zh-TW"}, severity}]}` (bin/lib/fm_ste.py:59, :221) to `ste_rules` [{id, en, "zh-TW"}] is done in the server. All text is escaped with the page's existing `esc`/`said`/`words` helpers.

Confirm questions on the page: each question has two buttons, 'Yes, correct' and 'No, change it' (dictionary words); choosing 'No, change it' opens a textarea (1-1000 code points, the same validation as today's custom text). For a card with questions, the existing Confirm order button stays disabled until every question has an answer (and every 'No' has valid text) and an option (or custom) is chosen; the existing pick/draft state handling and read-only/locked rules apply to the new controls. A card without questions behaves exactly as today. The POST body gains `answers: [{index, ok: true}|{index, ok: false, text}]` in question order only for cards with questions.

The server (board/server.ts POST /decisions, about :2159-2280): the request body may carry `answers`. When the pending record's `details.en.questions` exists, `answers` must be an array with exactly one entry per question, in order, each `{index, ok:true}` or `{index, ok:false, text}` with text validated like custom text; otherwise 400 with code `answersInvalid`. A card without questions refuses any non-empty `answers` with 400 `answersInvalid`. When every answer is ok:true, the decision is recorded and carried out exactly as today, with `answers` stored. When any answer is ok:false, the decision is a spec-change request and is stored so that no reader can take it for approval: `chosen: "change"` (a value no consumer treats as A/B/C/D or custom), `picked: <the option or 'custom' the captain selected>`, `answers`, `text` when the pick was custom, `effect: null`, `effect_outcome: "recorded"` (an existing value, so no new outcome value is introduced), `merge: null`; nothing is carried out (no merge, dispatch, park, drop or send_back), and decision_made is emitted with data {decision, chosen: 'change', picked, outcome: 'recorded'} and summaries `<id> change requested` / `<id> 要求修改`. Because every consumer that grants authority checks `chosen == 'A'` (bin/fm-ready.sh:172-178 `answered_a`, bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:109, :127, :254-262, bin/fm.sh:741-744 `adopt_proposal`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:53, bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py:252) or maps C/D (bin/fm-reconcile.sh:239-279), a 'change' record grants nothing and is never repaired as a park or drop; tests assert this for fm-ready (the task is not listed by `bin/fm-ready.sh cleared` for a change-requested readiness card), fm_spec_pins (no pin approval from a change record) and fm-reconcile (`bin/fm-reconcile.sh --repair-cards` reports nothing for it). Idempotency: a repeated post matches when the stored record has the same picked option, text and answers (for a change record) or the same chosen, text and answers (otherwise); a different post is 409 as today. Where the captain sees it: the post-answer toast (board/public/index.html, the outcome key chosen at about :813-816) uses a new dictionary key for a response whose stored `chosen` is 'change' (e.g. 'Change requested — firstmate revises the spec' / '已要求修改：firstmate 會修訂 spec'), instead of 'recorded'; for that response the toast shows only this message: feedbackText() (about :406-407) does not append the card's authored `outcome` (which describes carrying out an option), answer() (about :814-821) does not set the 'AYE, CAPTAIN! / ORDERS AWAY' cry and does not queue the 'order' ship animation, and observe() (about :424-433, called from render) skips outcomes whose `chosen` is 'change', so no tab (this one after its refetch at :822, or any other open tab) animates an order for a change answer; the e2e test asserts all three; the decision_made event's summary ('<id> change requested' / '<id> 要求修改') is what the activity log shows. The decision schema paragraph in design/design.md §5.2 (about :249-348, where `chosen` values are described) adds 'change', `picked` and `answers`. Firstmate is woken by the existing pushWake as today. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, section `## Author and verify captain decisions` (about :702-760), gets one sentence: an answer with chosen 'change' means revise the spec from the captain's answers, re-run preflight and raise a new card; never act on `picked`. Readers that only report `chosen` and grant nothing behave as follows for 'change', unchanged in code: bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:650 gives a wake reason only for B/C, so a 'change' answer gets no autopilot reason and firstmate is woken only by the board's pushWake (enough, because pushWake fires for every answer); bin/fm-herdr.py:2028-2096 replays answers and prints 'chose change' (the record's `picked` stays readable in the file); bin/lib/fm_watch.py:163 prints 'card: <id> answered change'; board/server.ts:1404 re-emits `chosen` into the outcomes list, which the page's observe() uses to queue a ship animation by identity and, after this task, skips for chosen 'change'; board/server.ts:1651 (merge settle) never runs for a 'change' record because its merge is null. Tests assert fm_watch's line for a 'change' record ('card: <id> answered change'), and the e2e test asserts the toast text for a change answer. Engine-wide view: board/server.ts builds `outcomes` (about :1402-1404) as {type, identity, data:{decision, chosen}} and, for an external project in the engine-wide view, reduces each entry to the allow-listed top-level plain values (about :1414-1448), which drops `data`. So every outcome entry (the decision_made events and the entries built from responses) also carries a top-level `chosen` copied from its data (the key `chosen` is already on that allow-list), and observe() reads `e.chosen ?? e.data?.chosen`; this way a 'change' outcome is skipped in a project's own view and in the engine-wide view alike. A test asserts that /api/state in the engine-wide view, with an external project whose decision is 'change', returns that outcome with top-level chosen 'change', and the e2e test asserts no order animation is queued from it.

Tests. tests/diagram.test.sh (1069 lines; stay under 1200, or add a new tests/diagram-nodes.test.sh): a record with before_nodes/after_nodes renders two SVGs with one rect per node in each language, the gone/new styles and marks, the legend, the change table, escaped labels (a label containing `<script>` appears escaped), zh-CN derived, including the SVG `<title>` text converted to simplified characters (a zh-TW label containing a character the tw2cn table maps appears converted in the zh-CN page); a record without nodes renders byte-identical to base (compare against the base output for the existing fixture); an authored tier still wins over nodes. Board: tests/e2e (Playwright, existing fixture tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts) — an intent card shows the intent sections, chips from `ste`, the STE pill; Confirm stays disabled until every question is answered; 'No, change it' requires text; a legacy card shows no new section. Server: tests/board-card-effects.test.sh (or a new board suite) — answers validated (missing, wrong count, bad text -> 400 answersInvalid; answers on a card without questions -> 400); all-yes answers carry the chosen effect as today; any 'No' stores `chosen: "change"` with `picked`, `answers`, `effect: null` and `effect_outcome: "recorded"`, carries no effect (a dispatch-effect card does not run fm-dispatch.sh: the existing stub records no call) and emits decision_made with data `chosen: "change"`, `picked` and `outcome: "recorded"`; repeated identical post is idempotent, a different one 409. i18n parity holds.

Docs, edited in place (T-189): design/design.md §8 'The captain's board' (design.md:1649), its subsection headed 'Interaction' (about :2176, which has no number of its own): the intent section, chips from the stored report, confirm questions and the change-request answer; §5.2 the paragraph on --details (about :359-367): one sentence that diagrams draw before_nodes/after_nodes in the built-in tier and that answers are recorded on the decision.

In flight. Pending cards without intent fields render and answer exactly as today; decisions already recorded are untouched. Depends on T-210 (fm_ste.py, the intent fields and the `ste` report); dispatched only after T-210 merges. No other open task edits board/public/index.html, board/server.ts or bin/fm-diagram.sh.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from the new diagram cases, the server answer cases and the e2e intent-card cases (red on base); the legacy-rendering and no-questions cases are regression guards, green on base and head. No vendor stub is involved.
